Lemma
[existence and uniqueness of a Jacobi field by its initial data, frame form]

↗ lem:dc-ch5-2-1-parallel-frame ↗ lem:dc-ch5-2-1-ode ↗ lem:dc-ch5-2-1-frame-reduction

1. ch5:2.1For every pair $(J_0,w_0)\in T_{\gamma (0)}M\times T_{\gamma (0)}M$, there is a unique Jacobi field $J$ along $\gamma $ such that $J(0)=J_0$ and $\frac{DJ}{dt}(0)=w_0$.
Proof

↗ lem:dc-ch5-2-1-parallel-frame ↗ lem:dc-ch5-2-1-ode ↗ lem:dc-ch5-2-1-frame-reduction \sketch Package the coefficients $a_{ij}(t)$ as a continuous operator field $A(t)$ acting on the coefficient vector $(f_i)$ by $(A(t)f)_j=\sum _i a_{ij}(t)f_i$. By section 1 the second-order linear system $f''+A(t)f=0$ has a solution with initial data $f_i(0)=\langle J_0,e_i(0)\rangle $, $f_i'(0)=\langle w_0,e_i(0)\rangle $, unique given that data. Put $J=\sum _i f_i e_i$. Pairing the Jacobi operator with the frame (section 1) expands $\frac{D^2J}{dt^2}+R(\gamma ',J)\gamma '=\sum _j\big(f_j''+\sum _i a_{ij}f_i\big)e_j=0$, so $J$ is a Jacobi field; the orthonormal expansion gives $J(0)=\sum _i\langle J_0,e_i(0)\rangle e_i(0)=J_0$, and the frame being parallel gives the initial velocity $w_0$. Uniqueness follows from uniqueness of the scalar system.

□
